proof_checks: C1 derives genuine differentiability and continuity of Frechet derivative. Continuous inverse Riesz map makes the actual gradient continuous; no gradient-continuity assumption or surrogate vector field is substituted.
Compact nonempty time interval plus continuous norm provides s in Icc 0 T and full IsMinOn comparison over that interval. Attainment is proved, not supplied.
Actual objective right derivative is obtained from HasFDerivAt f at X(u) composed with the supplied right derivative of X. Riesz inner product identity gives exactly minus gradient norm squared.
Minimality plus nonnegativity of norms yields m squared <= each gradient norm squared; negation gives the correct upper bound on objective derivative.

Existing right-slope Gronwall uses K=0, epsilon=-m squared, delta=f(X0), including final time T. Its scalar epsilon and delta may be arbitrary real, so negative forcing and negative objective values are permitted.

gronwallBound_K0 yields f(XT)<=f(X0)-T*m squared. Global minimality gives f(z)<=f(XT), hence m squared*T<=f(X0)-f(z). Division uses strict positive T. Square-root conversion uses nonnegative norm and nonnegative initial gap from global minimality.
Exact constant is sqrt((f(X0)-f(z))/T), with no factor 2, and full attained-minimum witness is preserved.
No ODE at T, no negative-time equation, no convexity/PL/Lipschitz bound, no ODE existence, no minimum existence proof, no terminal gradient estimate and no infinite-time convergence are claimed.
noncircularity: The theorem assumes only C1 objective, global minimum, continuous supplied trajectory and actual right gradient ODE. It derives both objective dissipation and small-gradient attained minimum. No supplied bound or scalar energy identity closes the result.
